## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Daddallavimānavatthu* (Vv 34), translated into English as "Dazzling Mansion", is a verse narrative within the *Vimānavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral]. The narrative centers on a conversation among devas concerning the superior merit of directing almsgiving toward the Noble Saṅgha as a whole rather than presenting gifts to individual monks [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral records passage-level parallels between the text and the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 17.9: *Navattabbaṁsaṁghassadinnaṁmahapphalantikathā*) as well as the *Vihāravimānavatthu* (Vv 44), noting also a relationship to the *Yajamānasutta* (SN 11.16) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus confirms substantial shared phrasing with Kv 17.9 (§20.1–26.4) and Vv 44 (§21.4–27.1), agreeing with the curated parallels [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects Pali-internal reuse across several other texts, including its commentary (*Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*), other *Vimānavatthu* accounts (Vv 29, Vv 33, and Vv 45), the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (*Aṭṭhakanipāta*, AN 8.60), the *Sakka Saṁyutta* (SN 11.16), the *Dasabrāhmaṇajātaka* (Ja 495), and the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus aligns sections of the text with the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) and two Tibetan canonical works (including D 494) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
